name: Veg Pulao
cuisine: North Indian (made across India as an everyday one-pot rice; a fixture of Mumbai Udupi and Punjabi restaurant menus)

ingredients.name: Basmati rice
ingredients.householdMeasure: A little over ⅓ cup (⅓ cup + 1 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Water (for cooking)
ingredients.householdMeasure: About ⅔ cup + 1 tbsp (open pan) / a little over ½ cup (cooker)

ingredients.name: Carrot (gajar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium carrot, diced small (about 3 tbsp)

ingredients.name: French beans (fansi)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 4–5 beans, cut into 1 cm pieces (about 2½ tbsp)

equipment: Small heavy-bottomed saucepan or kadai (1.5 litre) with a tight-fitting lid (open-pan method)
OR a 2–3 litre pressure cooker (see the note after the steps)
Mixing bowl for rinsing and soaking
Chopping board and knife; a peeler for the carrot (or scrape the skin with the back of the knife)
Measuring cup and spoons (a steel tumbler and ordinary teaspoons are fine; use the same cup for rice and water)
Flat spatula; a fork for fluffing

steps.title: Measure the rice
steps.text: Measure 75 g basmati rice (⅓ cup + 1 tbsp) into the bowl.
steps.visualCue: Long white grains, no stones or husks
steps.cameraCheck: The measured rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Rice pouring from the cup into the bowl.
steps.watchOut: Small stones or dark broken grains hiding in the rice; spread it on a plate and pick them out before rinsing.

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Cover with water, swirl gently with your fingers, pour off the cloudy water. Repeat 3–4 times.
steps.visualCue: The last rinse water is almost clear.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in nearly clear water
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling the rice, cloudy water draining away.
steps.watchOut: Rubbing the grains hard, which snaps basmati and gives a sticky pulao; swirl only, and stop when the water is faintly cloudy.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Cover the rinsed rice with about 1 cup fresh water and leave it for 20 minutes.
steps.visualCue: Grains turn opaque white and slightly plumper.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice soaking in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Still shot of the soaking rice, then a 20-min timer being set.
steps.watchOut: Soaking much longer than 30 minutes, which makes the grains fragile and mushy; set a timer. Short on time? Even 10 minutes helps.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Peel and thinly slice 40 g onion (½ small onion) into half-moons.
steps.visualCue: Thin, even slices that separate into strands
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced onion on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife slicing the onion half into thin strips.
steps.watchOut: Thick, uneven slices, which stay raw while thin ones burn; cut them to a similar thickness (about 3 mm).

steps.title: Dice the carrot
steps.text: Peel and dice 25 g carrot (¼ carrot) into small 0.5–1 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: Small orange cubes, all about the same size
steps.cameraCheck: About 3 tbsp diced carrot
steps.videoShot: Knife dicing a carrot strip into cubes.
steps.watchOut: Big chunks, which stay hard when the rice is done; if some are large, cut them again now.

steps.title: Cut the beans
steps.text: Top and tail 4–5 French beans (20 g) and cut them into 1 cm pieces.
steps.tip: Keep vegetable pieces small so they cook in the same time as the rice.
steps.visualCue: Short green pieces about the size of the carrot cubes
steps.cameraCheck: The cut beans on the board
steps.videoShot: Beans lined up and chopped in one go.
steps.watchOut: Leaving the stringy tips on, which feel tough in the finished pulao; snap both ends off first.

steps.title: Measure the peas
steps.text: Measure 2 tbsp (20 g) green peas. If frozen, rinse them under tap water to remove ice.
steps.visualCue: Bright green, separate peas
steps.cameraCheck: 2 tbsp peas in a bowl
steps.videoShot: Peas tipped into a small bowl.
steps.watchOut: Ice crystals on frozen peas, which add extra water to the pot; rinse and shake them dry.

steps.title: Prep the herbs and chilli
steps.text: Slit ½ green chilli lengthwise. Tear 8–10 mint leaves. Chop 2 tsp coriander leaves. Keep the coriander separate for garnish.
steps.visualCue: Slit chilli, torn mint, fine green coriander flecks
steps.cameraCheck: The chilli, mint and coriander in three small piles
steps.videoShot: Hands tearing mint leaves over the board.
steps.watchOut: Chopping the mint fine on the board, which bruises and blackens it; tear it by hand. Wash your hands after the chilli before touching your eyes.

steps.title: Measure the cooking water
steps.text: Measure 160 ml (about ⅔ cup + 1 tbsp) water and keep it near the stove.
steps.tip: This is a little under twice the volume of the dry rice; the vegetables add some water of their own.
steps.visualCue: Water at the line
steps.cameraCheck: The measuring cup of water
steps.videoShot: Water poured into the measuring cup.
steps.watchOut: Eyeballing the water, the most common reason for soggy or hard pulao; measure it with the same cup you used for the rice.

steps.title: Drain the rice
steps.text: Tip the soaked rice into the sieve and let it drip.
steps.visualCue: No more water dripping
steps.cameraCheck: The drained rice in the sieve
steps.videoShot: Water running out of the sieve.
steps.watchOut: Wet rice going into the pan, which spits hot ghee and turns gluey; shake the sieve once or twice until dripping stops.

steps.title: Heat the ghee
steps.text: Put the saucepan on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) ghee.
steps.visualCue: Ghee melts and shimmers; no smoke.
steps.cameraCheck: Melted ghee in the pan
steps.videoShot: Ghee melting and spreading across the pan.
steps.watchOut: Smoking ghee, which means the flame is too high and the spices will burn; lower the heat and wait a few seconds.

steps.title: Add the cumin seeds
steps.text: Add ½ tsp (1 g) cumin seeds.
steps.visualCue: They sizzle within a few seconds, darken one shade and smell nutty.
steps.cameraCheck: Sizzling cumin in the ghee
steps.videoShot: Cumin hitting the hot ghee and fizzing.
steps.watchOut: Black seeds and a bitter smell mean they burnt; wipe the pan and restart. No sizzle means the ghee is not hot yet.

steps.title: Add the whole spices
steps.text: Add the bay leaf, ½-inch cinnamon, 2 cloves, the cracked cardamom and 3 peppercorns. Stir once.
steps.visualCue: Cloves puff slightly, bay leaf darkens a shade; a warm, sweet smell rises.
steps.cameraCheck: The whole spices in the ghee
steps.videoShot: Spices dropping into the pan one by one.
steps.watchOut: Leaving them over 30 seconds, which scorches the cardamom and cinnamon and turns them bitter; go straight to the onion.

steps.title: Fry the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and stir often on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Soft, light golden at the edges, no dark brown bits
steps.cameraCheck: Golden onion in the pan
steps.videoShot: The spatula turning the onion as it colours.
steps.watchOut: Deep brown onion, which turns the pulao brown and bitter; if it darkens early, lower the heat and sprinkle 1 tbsp water.

steps.title: Add the ginger-garlic paste and chilli
steps.text: Add ½ tsp ginger-garlic paste and the slit chilli. Stir.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes and it smells cooked and sweet.
steps.cameraCheck: The paste mixed into the onion
steps.videoShot: Paste dropped in and stirred through.
steps.watchOut: Paste sticking and burning on the base; stir constantly and splash in 1 tbsp water if it catches.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, beans and peas. Stir and fry on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Colours brighten; the beans turn a deeper green and look glossy.
steps.cameraCheck: The vegetables in the pan
steps.videoShot: Orange, green and pale-green vegetables tossed together.
steps.watchOut: Frying so long the vegetables go soft before the rice goes in; 2 minutes is enough because they finish cooking with the rice.

steps.title: Add the mint
steps.text: Add the torn mint leaves and stir.
steps.visualCue: The leaves wilt and a fresh mint smell rises.
steps.cameraCheck: Wilted mint among the vegetables
steps.videoShot: Mint scattered over the vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Browned or blackened mint, a sign of too long on heat; add it only for the last 15 seconds before the rice.

steps.title: Add the drained rice
steps.text: Tip the drained rice into the pan.
steps.visualCue: The rice sits on top of the vegetables.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the pan
steps.videoShot: Rice sliding from the sieve into the pan.
steps.watchOut: Dumping it in a heap, which makes uneven coating; spread it across the pan.

steps.title: Sauté the rice gently
steps.text: Fold the rice gently from the bottom so every grain is coated in ghee.
steps.visualCue: Grains look glossy and dry, with no wet patches.
steps.cameraCheck: Glossy rice mixed with vegetables
steps.videoShot: The spatula lifting and folding the rice.
steps.watchOut: Stirring hard, which breaks the soaked grains into starchy mush; use slow folds and stop when the grains look dry and glossy.

steps.title: Add the water and salt
steps.text: Pour in the 160 ml water and add ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt. Stir gently once.
steps.tip: Taste the water: it should taste lightly salty, like mild soup.
steps.visualCue: Water just covers the rice by about 0.5 cm.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice under water in the pan
steps.videoShot: Water poured in, salt sprinkled.
steps.watchOut: Too little or too much water: grains showing above the surface means too little (add 2 tbsp hot water); more than 1 cm over the rice means too much (boil uncovered a minute longer in step 22).

steps.title: Bring to a boil
steps.text: Raise the heat to high, uncovered.
steps.visualCue: A rolling boil with bubbles across the surface.
steps.cameraCheck: The boiling pan
steps.videoShot: Bubbles breaking across the surface.
steps.watchOut: Stirring now, which releases starch and makes the rice sticky; leave it alone.

steps.title: Simmer until the surface water is gone
steps.text: Lower to medium and let it bubble uncovered, without stirring.
steps.visualCue: Water drops below the rice and small steam holes appear on the surface.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice surface with steam holes
steps.videoShot: Close-up of steam escaping through the holes.
steps.watchOut: Covering too soon (soggy top) or too late (dry, catching base); cover when you see the steam holes and no water pooling on top.

steps.title: Cover and cook on low
steps.text: Turn the flame to the lowest setting and cover tightly.
steps.visualCue: A faint, steady steam sound; no loud sizzling.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan on the lowest flame
steps.videoShot: Lid going on, knob turned down.
steps.watchOut: A burnt smell or loud crackling means the flame is too high or the pan is thin; move it to a tawa under the pan. Do not lift the lid during these 12 minutes.

steps.title: Check one grain
steps.text: Lift the lid, take a grain from the top and press it between your fingers. Tilt the pan to check the bottom.
steps.visualCue: The grain is soft right through, no hard white centre; no water pooled at the bottom.
steps.cameraCheck: A pressed grain on your fingertip
steps.videoShot: Fingers squashing a cooked grain.
steps.watchOut: A hard white centre: sprinkle 1–2 tbsp hot water, cover and cook 2–3 min more on low. Do not add cold water, which makes the grains gummy.

steps.title: Rest the pulao
steps.text: Switch off the heat and keep the lid on.
steps.visualCue: Grains firm up and stand upright.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan off the flame
steps.videoShot: Flame turned off, 5-min timer set.
steps.watchOut: Opening the lid early, which lets steam out and leaves the top wet; wait the full 5 minutes.

steps.title: Fluff the pulao
steps.text: Remove the lid and gently lift the grains with a fork, from the sides towards the centre.
steps.tip: Pick out the bay leaf, cinnamon and cloves now if you do not want to bite into them.
steps.visualCue: Long, separate grains with vegetables spread through
steps.cameraCheck: The fluffed pulao in the pan
steps.videoShot: The fork lifting airy grains and vegetables.
steps.watchOut: Mashing with a spoon, which breaks the grains; use a fork and lift, not press.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle the chopped coriander and fold once.
steps.visualCue: White rice dotted with orange, green and fresh coriander
steps.cameraCheck: The served plate
steps.videoShot: Coriander falling on the pulao, then a slow pan across the plate.
steps.watchOut: Adding coriander early so it cooks to grey; add it only now.

reasons: it is not fried, uses only 2 tsp ghee, and the vegetables lift fibre to about 5 g; sodium is moderate (about 600 mg, around 30% of the daily limit). But it is still mostly refined white rice with only about 8 g protein, so on its own it is light on protein. Restaurant versions commonly use 2–3 tbsp ghee or oil per cup of rice, add cashews and sometimes butter or cream, use more salt, and serve a bigger portion with fewer vegetables, which can push it past 550–650 kcal (est.).

researchRating.basis: veg pulao is one of the most-cooked Indian rice dishes and a lunchbox staple, and the recipe pages seen this run score 4.2–5 (Tarla Dalal 5.0 from 3 reviews; Cupofyum 4.8 from 12; Green Bowl 2 Soul 5 from 16; Spice Up The Curry 4.6 from 23 on Slurrp; Whiskaffair 4.38 from 24; Hebbar's Kitchen 4.2 from 29 on Slurrp; Rachna Cooks 5 from 4). Counts are small and the sites use different systems. It loses a little because it is often seen as a simple everyday rice, and reviewers often mention mushy or bland results.

storage: Cool quickly (spread on a plate) and refrigerate in an airtight box within 1 hour of cooking; cooked rice can carry *Bacillus cereus* spores, which multiply if it sits warm. Keeps 1–2 days in the fridge (3 at most). Freezer: yes, flattened in a zip bag or box, up to 1 month (peas and carrot freeze well; beans soften a little). Reheat only once: sprinkle 1–2 tsp water and microwave covered 1–2 min, stirring halfway, or steam in a covered pan on low for 3–4 min, until piping hot.
leftoverRemix: Pulao cutlets. Mash 1 cup cold leftover pulao with 1 small boiled potato, 2 tbsp besan or breadcrumbs, a pinch of chilli powder and garam masala, and chopped coriander. Shape into 4 flat patties and shallow-fry on a tawa with 1 tsp oil, 2–3 min per side, until crisp. Serve with green chutney or ketchup. (Quick alternative: toss the pulao on a hot tawa with ½ tsp pav bhaji masala, chopped tomato and capsicum, and a squeeze of lemon.)
burnOff: about 6.1 km of running (424 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.5 km of brisk walking (about 1 hr 40 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With a bowl of raita (about 500 kcal in total): about 7 km running or 10 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: rice is a grain avoided on the common vrat rule set, and the recipe has onion and garlic; the usual swap is samak (barnyard millet) with sendha namak (rock salt) and no onion or garlic (common rule set assumed; samak version not researched)

ekadashi.reason: rice is the grain most strictly avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set (families differ)

jain.reason: drop onion, ginger-garlic paste and carrot (all root vegetables) and use sonth instead; see Jain variant

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; a filling side or light main at iftar, but protein is only about 8 g and sodium about 600 mg, so pair with curd raita or dal

jain.reason: drop the onion (40 g), ginger-garlic paste and carrot, use sonth (dry ginger powder) and allowed vegetables (see Jain variant)

vegan.reason: swap the ghee (10 g) for neutral oil (see Vegan variant)

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian recipe with no meat or egg

sattvik.reason: skip the onion and ginger-garlic paste (see Jain variant, which also covers this)

glutenFree.reason: rice, vegetables and whole spices only; no hing is used (most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so do not add it)

dairyFree.reason: swap the ghee (10 g) for oil (see Vegan variant); nothing else has dairy

variants.name: Jain green vegetable pulao (no onion, garlic or root vegetables)
Veg pulao with oil instead of ghee (also the dairy-free variant)

variants.reason: Main recipe already gluten-free (no hing used; keep it out, since most hing sold in India contains wheat flour).
